# About this qmd {.unnumbered}

This is the first version of the PUMA dataset, built around 2024
overdose deaths and the 2020–2024 ACS 5-year sample. The main analysis
now uses the 2022–2024 dataset. It also keeps the earlier exploratory
work on exposure measures (inverse-distance weighting with K nearest
prisons or a fixed radius, including versions where K or the radius was
chosen by best fit). Those fit-selected measures aren't used in the main
analysis.

Data:

-   IPUMS USA, 2020–2024 ACS 5-year sample (`us2024c`): controls and
    divorce outcomes, with people in institutions (including prisoners)
    removed. Every respondent in this sample is coded to a 2020 PUMA.
-   2020 decennial census tract populations: weights for turning tract
    values (CDC rates, RUCA codes) into PUMA values.
-   CDC tract-level death rates for 2024 (overdose, suicide, homicide).
-   USDA RUCA codes (2020 tracts) and HIFLD/ICPSR prison boundaries.

The slow downloads (IPUMS extract, tract populations) happen only the
first time; after that the saved files are read. The first run needs an
IPUMS API key and a Census API key.

Outputs: `data/final/national_puma_dataset.csv` and
`data/final/rural_puma_dataset.csv`. Read `GEOID20` and `state_fips`
back as text so the leading zeros survive.

Units: shares are percentages (0–100). Exceptions are death rates (per
100,000), distances (km), land area (km²), density (people per km²),
median income (2024 dollars), counts, logs, and the inverse-distance
measures (sum of 1/(km + 1), no natural unit).

# Setup {#sec-setup}

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)   
library(sf)          
library(tidycensus)  
library(tigris)     
library(nngeo)       
library(gt)          
library(broom)       
library(fixest)      
library(ipumsr)      

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)  # cache downloaded shapefiles between sessions
```

# Building the dataset {#sec-build}

## IPUMS ACS microdata (2020–2024 5-year)

The first run requests the extract from IPUMS and saves the microdata as
`data/raw/data_ipums_2024.csv` and the codebook as `data/ddi.rds`. After
that it just reads the saved files.

```{r}
#| label: ipums-extract
# Download the extract the first time and save it; after that, read the saved files.
# Delete the two saved files to request a new extract (e.g. after adding variables).
ipums_csv <- "data/raw/data_ipums_2024.csv"
ipums_ddi <- "data/ddi.rds"

if (!file.exists(ipums_csv)) {
  extract_def <- define_extract_micro(
    collection  = "usa",
    description = "Non-institutionalized population by 2020 PUMA, 2020-2024 ACS 5-year",
    samples     = "us2024c",   # 2020-2024 ACS 5-year; all records coded to 2020 PUMAs
    variables   = c(
      "STATEFIP", "PUMA",                # geography: state + 2020 PUMA
      "PERWT", "HHWT", "PERNUM",         # person weight, household weight, person number in household
      "GQTYPE",                          # group-quarters type (to drop institutions, incl. prisons)
      "AGE", "RACE", "HISPAN",           # demographics
      "MARST", "DIVINYR",                # marital status, divorced in past 12 months
      "EDUC",                            # educational attainment
      "POVERTY",                         # family income as % of poverty line
      "EMPSTAT",                         # employed / unemployed / not in labor force
      "HHINCOME"                         # total household income (2024 dollars in this sample)
    )
  )

  extract_submitted <- submit_extract(extract_def)
  extract_complete  <- wait_for_extract(extract_submitted)
  path <- download_extract(extract_complete, download_dir = "data")

  ddi <- read_ipums_ddi(path)                  # codebook (variable labels, value labels)
  data_ipums_2024 <- read_ipums_micro(ddi)     # one row per person (roughly 16 million rows)

  write_csv(data_ipums_2024, ipums_csv)
  saveRDS(ddi, ipums_ddi)
}

# The CSV keeps the numeric codes but not the labels, so the labels come from ddi
data_ipums_2024 <- read_csv(ipums_csv)
ddi <- readRDS(ipums_ddi)
```

### Codes and the institutional population

The public ACS doesn't separate prisons from other institutions, so
nursing-home residents are dropped along with prisoners.

```{r}
#| label: ipums-codes
# Labels come from the codebook (ddi, loaded above), since the CSV has codes only.
ipums_val_labels(ddi, GQTYPE)    # 1-4 = institutions (prisons, nursing homes, etc.)
ipums_val_labels(ddi, MARST)     # 1-3 = married/separated, 4 = divorced
ipums_val_labels(ddi, DIVINYR)   # 1 = No, 2 = Yes, 0/8 = outside universe / suppressed
ipums_val_labels(ddi, EMPSTAT)   # 1 = employed, 2 = unemployed, 3 = not in labor force
ipums_val_labels(ddi, EDUC)      # 10 = 4 years of college, 11 = 5+ years
ipums_val_labels(ddi, RACE)      # 1 = White
ipums_val_labels(ddi, HISPAN)    # 0 = Not Hispanic, 9 = Not reported

# Remove everyone living in an institution. The public ACS doesn't separate prisons
# from other institutions, so nursing-home residents are removed too. 
data_noninst <- data_ipums_2024 %>%
  filter(!GQTYPE %in% c(1, 2, 3, 4))

# 7-digit PUMA ID (2-digit state + 5-digit PUMA), matching GEOID20 in the boundary file
data_noninst <- data_noninst %>%
  mutate(puma_geoid = paste0(sprintf("%02d", STATEFIP), sprintf("%05d", PUMA)))
```

### PUMA-level variables

```{r}
#| label: ipums-puma
# Pattern used throughout: sum(PERWT[condition]) is the weighted number of people
# meeting the condition; dividing two of these and multiplying by 100 gives a percentage.
# In a 5-year sample the weights add up to the average population over 2020-2024.

# Person-level variables 
puma_person <- data_noninst %>%
  group_by(puma_geoid) %>%
  summarise(
    # Population (non-institutionalized)
    total_pop = sum(PERWT),

    # Race: % whose race is not White (Hispanic Whites count as White).  
    pct_nonwhite    = 100 * (1 - sum(PERWT[RACE == 1]) / sum(PERWT)),
    # Alternative: % who are not non-Hispanic White (excludes HISPAN "not reported")
    pct_nonwhite_nh = 100 * (1 - sum(PERWT[RACE == 1 & HISPAN == 0]) / sum(PERWT[HISPAN != 9])),

    # Education: % of people 25+ with a bachelor's degree or more
    pct_bachelors_plus = 100 * sum(PERWT[EDUC >= 10 & AGE >= 25]) / sum(PERWT[AGE >= 25]),

    # Poverty: % below the poverty line, among people with a poverty status.
    # POVERTY = 0 means N/A (e.g. college dorms), so it's excluded from both parts.
    pct_poverty = 100 * sum(PERWT[POVERTY > 0 & POVERTY < 100]) / sum(PERWT[POVERTY > 0]),

    # Unemployment: % of the labor force (employed + unemployed) that is unemployed.
    # EMPSTAT covers people 16+. Note: members of the armed forces count as employed here.
    pct_unemployed = 100 * sum(PERWT[EMPSTAT == 2]) / sum(PERWT[EMPSTAT %in% c(1, 2)]),

    # Divorce outcome
    # Main outcome: % of ever-married people (15+) who divorced in the past 12 months.
    pct_divorced_past_yr = 100 * sum(PERWT[DIVINYR == 2]) / sum(PERWT[DIVINYR %in% c(1, 2)]),
    # Alternative: % of people "at risk" of divorce (currently married/separated, or divorced
    # in the past year). The "|" counts each person once, so a divorce-then-remarriage isn't double-counted.
    pct_divorced_past_yr_atrisk = 100 * sum(PERWT[DIVINYR == 2]) / sum(PERWT[MARST %in% 1:3 | DIVINYR == 2]),
    # Stock measure: % of people 15+ currently divorced
    pct_currently_divorced = 100 * sum(PERWT[MARST == 4 & AGE >= 15]) / sum(PERWT[AGE >= 15]),

    # Unweighted sample sizes, to judge how reliable each PUMA's divorce rate is
    n_person_sample   = n(),
    n_divorced_sample = sum(DIVINYR == 2)
  )

# Median household income (household level)
# Income is a household property, so use one record per household (PERNUM == 1) and the
# household weight HHWT. HHINCOME = 9999999 means N/A (people in group quarters).
# In IPUMS multi-year samples, dollar amounts are already in final-year (2024) dollars.
weighted_median <- function(x, w) {
  x <- as.numeric(x); w <- as.numeric(w)
  o <- order(x)
  cum_share <- cumsum(w[o]) / sum(w)
  x[o][which(cum_share >= 0.5)[1]]   # first value at or past half the weight
}

puma_household <- data_noninst %>%
  filter(PERNUM == 1, HHINCOME != 9999999) %>%
  group_by(puma_geoid) %>%
  summarise(
    medhhinc   = weighted_median(HHINCOME, HHWT),
    n_hh_sample = n()
  )

# Combine and add logged versions used in the models 
puma_summary <- puma_person %>%        # puma_summary - all ipums vars in the final form
  left_join(puma_household, by = "puma_geoid") %>%
  mutate(
    log_pop      = log(total_pop),
    log_medhhinc = log(medhhinc)
  )

nrow(puma_summary)                      # should be 2462 (50 states + DC)
```

## PUMA boundaries

```{r}
#| label: puma-geography
# Download cartographic-boundary PUMA polygons for the 50 states + DC.
# fips_codes lists states first, so the first 51 unique codes are 50 states + DC
# (territories such as Puerto Rico come after and are excluded).
state_fips <- unique(tidycensus::fips_codes$state_code)[1:51]

pumas_2020 <- map_dfr(state_fips, function(st) {
  pumas(state = st, cb = TRUE, year = 2020)
})

nrow(pumas_2020)
names(pumas_2020)   # look for GEOID20

# Start the master PUMA table: boundaries + IPUMS aggregates.
puma_final <- pumas_2020 %>%.       # puma_final - geography, geoid + ipums variables
  left_join(puma_summary, by = c("GEOID20" = "puma_geoid"))

nrow(puma_final)                    # should still be 2462
sum(is.na(puma_final$total_pop))    # PUMAs with no match in your microdata
```

## Tract populations (2020 census)

The CDC rates and RUCA codes are reported for tracts, and each PUMA is
made up of whole tracts. To get one PUMA value from many tract values I
average them weighted by tract population. The 2020 census is used
because its tract IDs match `rel20` and the RUCA file exactly.

```{r}
#| label: tract-pop
# 2020 census tract populations. Downloaded the first time (needs a Census API key for
# tidycensus) and saved; after that the saved file is read. GEOID is read as text so the
# leading zeros survive and the IDs match rel20.
tract_pop_file <- "data/raw/tract_pop_2020.csv"
if (!file.exists(tract_pop_file)) {
  tract_pop_2020 <- map_dfr(state_fips, function(st) {
    get_decennial(
      geography = "tract", state = st, year = 2020, sumfile = "pl",
      variables = c(tot_pop          = "P1_001N",   # total population (the weight)
                    pop_inst_gq      = "P5_002N",   # people in institutional group quarters
                    pop_correctional = "P5_003N"),  # people in adult correctional facilities
      output = "wide")
  }) %>%
    select(GEOID, tot_pop, pop_inst_gq, pop_correctional)
  write_csv(tract_pop_2020, tract_pop_file)
}
tract_pop_2020 <- read_csv(tract_pop_file, col_types = cols(GEOID = col_character()))

nrow(tract_pop_2020)                    # ~84,000 tracts
all(nchar(tract_pop_2020$GEOID) == 11)  # every ID should be an 11-digit tract code
```

## Death rates (CDC, tract level)

```{r}
#| label: deaths-tract
# CDC death rates (per 100,000) for drug overdose, suicide, homicide and firearm
# injuries, by census tract of residence, for several periods. Only 2024 is kept below.
injury_overdose_violence <- read_csv("data/raw/injury_overdose_violence_census_tract.csv")

# Small tracts are pooled in the source file: NAME holds a comma-separated list of
# the tracts sharing one rate. separate_rows() gives each real tract its own row,
# each carrying the pooled rate.
injury_overdose_violence_exploded <- injury_overdose_violence %>%
  separate_rows(NAME, sep = ",\\s*") %>% #split combined tract lists into one row per real tract
  rename(real_tract_geoid = NAME) %>%
  mutate(real_tract_geoid = str_trim(real_tract_geoid))

# These should now be clean 11-digit real Census tract GEOIDs
head(injury_overdose_violence_exploded$real_tract_geoid, 10)
nchar(injury_overdose_violence_exploded$real_tract_geoid[1])

# 2024 only, three intents, reshaped wide: one row per tract, one column per rate.
# -999 marks suppressed values and is converted to NA.
injury_overdose_violence_2024 <- injury_overdose_violence_exploded %>%
  filter(Period == "2024") %>%
  filter(Intent %in% c("Drug_OD", "All_Suicide", "All_Homicide")) %>%
  mutate(Rate = as.numeric(Rate)) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols    = c(real_tract_geoid, ST_GEOID, ST_NAME, Period),
    names_from  = Intent,
    values_from = Rate,
    names_glue  = "{Intent}_rate"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    overdose_rate = Drug_OD_rate,
    suicide_rate  = All_Suicide_rate,
    homicide_rate = All_Homicide_rate,
    GEOID = real_tract_geoid,
    year = Period
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(year),
    suicide_rate  = ifelse(suicide_rate  == -999, NA, suicide_rate),
    homicide_rate = ifelse(homicide_rate == -999, NA, homicide_rate),
    overdose_rate = ifelse(overdose_rate == -999, NA, overdose_rate)
  )

nrow(injury_overdose_violence_2024)
n_distinct(injury_overdose_violence_2024$GEOID)   # should equal nrow() if one row per tract
```

### Tracts to PUMAs

```{r}
#| label: deaths-puma
# Tract -> 2020 PUMA crosswalk (official Census relationship file)
rel20_raw <- read_csv("https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/maps-data/data/rel2020/2020_Census_Tract_to_2020_PUMA.txt",
                      col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

# rel20: GEOID = 11-digit tract ID, GEOID20 = 7-digit 2020 PUMA ID.
# Reused later in the Rurality section.
rel20 <- rel20_raw %>%
  transmute(
    GEOID   = paste0(STATEFP, COUNTYFP, TRACTCE),
    GEOID20 = paste0(STATEFP, PUMA5CE)
  )

# Attach PUMA and tract population (weights) to the exploded CDC data 
# tract_pop_2020 comes from the 2020 decennial census (section "Tract populations").
tract_outcomes <- injury_overdose_violence_2024 %>%
  select(GEOID, overdose_rate, suicide_rate, homicide_rate) %>%
  left_join(rel20, by = "GEOID") %>%
  left_join(tract_pop_2020 %>% select(GEOID, tot_pop), by = "GEOID")

# Checks before aggregating
anyDuplicated(tract_outcomes$GEOID)              # 0 => each tract appears once
mean(!is.na(tract_outcomes$GEOID20))             # share of CDC tracts matched to a PUMA
mean(!is.na(tract_outcomes$tot_pop))             # share with population weights

# Population-weighted aggregation to PUMA
# A PUMA's rate = average of its tracts' rates, weighted by tract population.
# These stay as deaths per 100,000 (the CDC's unit)
puma_outcomes <- tract_outcomes %>%
  filter(!is.na(GEOID20), !is.na(tot_pop), tot_pop > 0) %>%
  group_by(GEOID20) %>%
  summarise(
    overdose_rate_puma  = weighted.mean(overdose_rate,  tot_pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    suicide_rate_puma   = weighted.mean(suicide_rate,   tot_pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    homicide_rate_puma  = weighted.mean(homicide_rate,  tot_pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Coverage: % of the PUMA's population living in tracts with a non-missing overdose rate
    pct_pop_with_overdose_data = 100 * sum(tot_pop[!is.na(overdose_rate)]) / sum(tot_pop),
    n_tracts = n()
  )

# Join onto your PUMA dataset 
puma_final <- puma_final %>%
  left_join(puma_outcomes, by = "GEOID20")

nrow(puma_final)                               # still 2462
sum(is.na(puma_final$overdose_rate_puma))      # PUMAs with no overdose data at all
summary(puma_final$pct_pop_with_overdose_data)
```

## Rurality (RUCA codes)

```{r}
#| label: ruca
# Read the RUCA file with every column as text. FIPS codes have leading zeros,
# and reading them as numbers would strip the zero.
ruca_raw <- read_csv("data/raw/rurality/RUCA-codes-2020-tract.csv", col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

# Each tract's 2020 ID and its primary RUCA code (1-10, or 99 for "not coded").
ruca <- ruca_raw %>%
  transmute(GEOID = TractFIPS20, ruca = as.numeric(PrimaryRUCA))

# Every tract with its population, its PUMA, and its RUCA code. 
# Weights are total 2020 census population, which includes people in prisons.
tract_ruca <- tract_pop_2020 %>%
  select(GEOID, tot_pop) %>%
  left_join(rel20, by = "GEOID") %>%
  left_join(ruca,  by = "GEOID")

# Share of tracts that found a PUMA and a RUCA code
mean(!is.na(tract_ruca$GEOID20))
mean(!is.na(tract_ruca$ruca))

puma_rural_ruca <- tract_ruca %>%
  # Drop tracts with no PUMA, no RUCA code, the "not coded" category (99), or zero population
  filter(!is.na(GEOID20), !is.na(ruca), ruca != 99, tot_pop > 0) %>%
  group_by(GEOID20) %>%
  summarise(
    # % of the PUMA's population living in each type of tract
    pct_pop_metro      = 100 * sum(tot_pop[ruca %in% 1:3]) / sum(tot_pop),  # metropolitan
    pct_pop_micro      = 100 * sum(tot_pop[ruca %in% 4:6]) / sum(tot_pop),  # micropolitan
    pct_pop_small_town = 100 * sum(tot_pop[ruca %in% 7:9]) / sum(tot_pop),  # small town
    pct_pop_rural      = 100 * sum(tot_pop[ruca == 10])     / sum(tot_pop)   # rural  
  )

puma_final <- puma_final %>%
  left_join(puma_rural_ruca, by = "GEOID20")

nrow(puma_final)                         # should still be 2462
sum(is.na(puma_final$pct_pop_rural))     # PUMAs without a rurality value
summary(puma_final$pct_pop_rural)
```

## Analysis dataset

```{r}
#| label: puma-df
# puma_final already holds everything (IPUMS, deaths, rurality); drop the geometry
# and add helper columns.
puma_df <- puma_final %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  mutate(
    pct_pop_nonmetro = 100 - pct_pop_metro,   # used to define the rural subsample
    state_fips       = substr(GEOID20, 1, 2), # used to cluster standard errors

    # Area: ALAND20 is the official land area in square meters (water excluded)
    land_area_km2    = as.numeric(ALAND20) / 1e6,

    # Population density: non-institutionalized residents (IPUMS) per km2 of land
    pop_density      = total_pop / land_area_km2,
    log_pop_density  = log(pop_density)       # density is very skewed; use the log in models
  )

nrow(puma_df)                             # should be 2462
```

Share of each PUMA's land area (rather than population) in non-metro
tracts, used for the alternative rural definitions.

```{r}
#| label: rural-area
# % of each PUMA's land area in non-metro tracts, and three rural flags
tract_land <- map_dfr(state_fips, ~ tracts(state = .x, year = 2020, cb = TRUE)) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  transmute(GEOID, aland_km2 = ALAND / 1e6)      # land area, excluding water

puma_rural_area <- tract_ruca %>%
  filter(!is.na(GEOID20), !is.na(ruca), ruca != 99) %>%
  left_join(tract_land, by = "GEOID") %>%
  filter(!is.na(aland_km2), aland_km2 > 0) %>%
  group_by(GEOID20) %>%
  summarise(pct_area_nonmetro = 100 * sum(aland_km2[ruca >= 4]) / sum(aland_km2),
            .groups = "drop")

puma_df <- puma_df %>%
  left_join(puma_rural_area, by = "GEOID20") %>%
  mutate(rural_pop   = pct_pop_nonmetro  > 50,
         rural_area  = pct_area_nonmetro > 50,
         rural_both  = rural_pop & rural_area)

table(pop = puma_df$rural_pop, area = puma_df$rural_area, useNA = "ifany")
```

## Prison exposure

All measures use open state and federal prisons only, with distances
from each PUMA's geographic centroid.

| Measure | How it's built |
|----|----|
| `prison_present`, `num_prisons` | prisons inside the PUMA boundary |
| `dist_to_nearest_prison_km` | centroid to the closest prison |
| `num_prisons_within_5km`, `_10km` | prisons within 5 / 10 km of the centroid |
| IDW | sum of 1/(km + 1) over a set of prisons (0 km → 1.0, 4 km → 0.2, 49 km → 0.02) |
| IDW, K nearest | the K nearest prisons: K = 5, or K chosen by best fit |
| IDW, radius | every prison within R km: R = 50 and 10, or R chosen by best fit |

"Chosen by best fit" - the one with the lowest AIC.

### Counts, nearest distance, fixed-K IDW

```{r}
#| label: prison-exposure
# PUMA polygons and centroids in a meters-based CRS (EPSG:5070, CONUS Albers)
pumas_proj     <- st_transform(pumas_2020, 5070)
puma_centroids <- st_centroid(pumas_proj)

# Prisons: OPEN STATE and FEDERAL facilities only, as points 
# Every measure below uses this set and nothing else.
prisons_icpsr <- st_read("data/raw/prison-boundaries-1-geojson.geojson") %>%
  st_make_valid()

prisons_open_pts <- prisons_icpsr %>%
  filter(STATUS == "OPEN", TYPE %in% c("STATE", "FEDERAL")) %>%
  st_centroid() %>%
  st_transform(5070)

nrow(prisons_open_pts)          # should be 2005
table(prisons_open_pts$TYPE)

# Number of prisons inside each PUMA, and presence (0/1) 
prisons_by_puma <- st_join(prisons_open_pts, pumas_proj["GEOID20"], join = st_within) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(!is.na(GEOID20)) %>%
  count(GEOID20, name = "num_prisons")

# Distances from each PUMA centroid to its 20 nearest prisons 
# Computed once and reused for the nearest-distance and both IDW measures.
# st_nn() returns them sorted from nearest to farthest, in meters.
K_max <- 20
nn <- st_nn(puma_centroids, prisons_open_pts, k = K_max, returnDist = TRUE, progress = FALSE)
dist_km <- lapply(nn$dist, function(d) d / 1000)   # list: one vector of 20 distances (km) per PUMA

# Distance to the nearest prison (km)
puma_centroids$dist_to_nearest_prison_km <- sapply(dist_km, function(d) d[1])

# Number of prisons within 5 km and 10 km of the centroid 
puma_centroids$num_prisons_within_5km  <- lengths(st_is_within_distance(puma_centroids, prisons_open_pts, dist = 5000))
puma_centroids$num_prisons_within_10km <- lengths(st_is_within_distance(puma_centroids, prisons_open_pts, dist = 10000))

# Inverse-distance-weighted exposure, fixed K (K_fixed below)
# Sum of 1 / (km + 1) over the K nearest prisons; closer prisons count more.
idw <- function(K) sapply(dist_km, function(d) sum(1 / (d[1:K] + 1)))
idw_for_K <- function(K) tibble(GEOID20 = puma_centroids$GEOID20, idw_k = idw(K))

K_fixed <- 5
puma_centroids$prison_exposure_idw <- idw(K_fixed)

# Assemble and add to puma_df
puma_exposure <- puma_centroids %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(GEOID20, dist_to_nearest_prison_km, num_prisons_within_5km,
         num_prisons_within_10km, prison_exposure_idw) %>%
  left_join(prisons_by_puma, by = "GEOID20") %>%
  mutate(
    num_prisons    = replace_na(num_prisons, 0),     # PUMAs with no prison inside get 0, not NA
    prison_present = as.integer(num_prisons > 0)
  )

# Remove any exposure columns already in puma_df (from an earlier run, or from older
# versions of this chunk) so re-running doesn't create .x / .y duplicates
old_cols <- c("num_prisons", "prison_present", "capacity_total", "pop_total",
              "dist_to_nearest_prison_km", "num_prisons_within_5km", "num_prisons_within_10km",
              "num_prisons_within_25km", "num_prisons_within_50km", "mean_dist_3_nearest_km",
              "prison_exposure_idw", "prison_exposure_idw_auto_od", "prison_exposure_idw_auto_div")

puma_df <- puma_df %>%
  select(-any_of(old_cols)) %>%
  left_join(puma_exposure, by = "GEOID20")

nrow(puma_df)                      # still 2462
table(puma_df$prison_present)
summary(puma_df$prison_exposure_idw)
```

### IDW with K chosen by fit

```{r}
#| label: prison-idw-auto-k
# Inverse-distance-weighted exposure, K chosen by the data 
# For each K from 1 to 20, fit the full model and record its AIC; keep the K with the lowest AIC.
# Selection uses the national sample; the chosen K is also used for the rural dataset.
# `controls` must match the control set used in the analysis notebook.
controls <- "pct_nonwhite + log_medhhinc + pct_poverty + pct_unemployed + pct_pop_rural + pct_bachelors_plus + log_pop"

choose_K <- function(outcome) {
  fml <- as.formula(paste(outcome, "~ idw_k +", controls))
  map_dfr(1:K_max, function(K) {
    d <- puma_df %>% left_join(idw_for_K(K), by = "GEOID20")
    m <- feols(fml, data = d, cluster = ~state_fips)
    tibble(K = K, AIC = AIC(m), n = nobs(m))
  })
}

k_search_od  <- choose_K("overdose_rate_puma")
k_search_div <- choose_K("pct_divorced_past_yr")

K_auto_od  <- k_search_od$K[which.min(k_search_od$AIC)]
K_auto_div <- k_search_div$K[which.min(k_search_div$AIC)]
K_auto_od; K_auto_div              # the selected K for each outcome

# How fit changes with K (a flat curve means the choice of K hardly matters)
ggplot(k_search_od, aes(K, AIC)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Overdose model: AIC by K (lower = better)")

puma_df <- puma_df %>%
  select(-any_of(c("prison_exposure_idw_auto_od", "prison_exposure_idw_auto_div"))) %>%
  left_join(idw_for_K(K_auto_od)  %>% rename(prison_exposure_idw_auto_od  = idw_k), by = "GEOID20") %>%
  left_join(idw_for_K(K_auto_div) %>% rename(prison_exposure_idw_auto_div = idw_k), by = "GEOID20")
```

Quick checks on whether prison exposure improves fit at all (these are
exploratory):

```{r}
#| label: check-aic-no-prison
# AIC of the divorce model with no prison variable, to compare with the K search
  AIC(feols(as.formula(paste("pct_divorced_past_yr ~", controls)), data = puma_df, cluster = ~state_fips))
```

```{r}
#| label: check-m0-vs-m13
# Divorce model without vs. with the automatic-K exposure (state-clustered SEs)
m0  <- feols(as.formula(paste("pct_divorced_past_yr ~", controls)), data = puma_df, cluster = ~state_fips)
m13 <- feols(as.formula(paste("pct_divorced_past_yr ~ prison_exposure_idw_auto_od +", controls)),
             data = puma_df, cluster = ~state_fips)

etable(m0, m13, fitstat = ~ r2 + aic + n)   # side by side: coefficients, clustered SEs, R², AIC, N
```

### IDW within a radius

```{r}
#| label: prison-idw-radius
# Distance from every PUMA centroid to every prison (km)
# Rows = PUMAs (same order as puma_centroids), columns = prisons.
D_km <- matrix(as.numeric(st_distance(puma_centroids, prisons_open_pts)) / 1000,
               nrow = nrow(puma_centroids))

# Sum of 1 / (km + 1) over all prisons within R km; PUMAs with none in range get 0.
idw_radius <- function(R) rowSums((D_km <= R) * (1 / (D_km + 1)))
idw_for_R  <- function(R) tibble(GEOID20 = puma_centroids$GEOID20, idw_r = idw_radius(R))

# How many prisons each PUMA "sees" at a given radius (this is the K that varies)
n_within <- function(R) rowSums(D_km <= R)
summary(n_within(50)); summary(n_within(100))

# Version 1: radius chosen by me
R_fixed <- 50   # km
puma_df <- puma_df %>%
  select(-any_of(c("prison_exposure_idw_r50", "n_prisons_within_r50"))) %>%
  left_join(idw_for_R(R_fixed) %>% rename(prison_exposure_idw_r50 = idw_r), by = "GEOID20") %>%
  left_join(tibble(GEOID20 = puma_centroids$GEOID20, n_prisons_within_r50 = n_within(R_fixed)),
            by = "GEOID20")

# Version 2: radius chosen by the lowest AIC
R_values <- c(5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 300)

choose_R <- function(outcome) {
  fml <- as.formula(paste(outcome, "~ idw_r +", controls))
  map_dfr(R_values, function(R) {
    d <- puma_df %>% left_join(idw_for_R(R), by = "GEOID20")
    m <- feols(fml, data = d, cluster = ~state_fips)
    tibble(R = R, AIC = AIC(m), n = nobs(m))
  })
}

r_search_od  <- choose_R("overdose_rate_puma")
r_search_div <- choose_R("pct_divorced_past_yr")

R_auto_od  <- r_search_od$R[which.min(r_search_od$AIC)]
R_auto_div <- r_search_div$R[which.min(r_search_div$AIC)]
R_auto_od; R_auto_div

ggplot(r_search_od, aes(R, AIC)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Overdose model: AIC by radius (lower = better)", x = "Radius (km)")

puma_df <- puma_df %>%
  select(-any_of(c("prison_exposure_idw_r_auto_od", "prison_exposure_idw_r_auto_div"))) %>%
  left_join(idw_for_R(R_auto_od)  %>% rename(prison_exposure_idw_r_auto_od  = idw_r), by = "GEOID20") %>%
  left_join(idw_for_R(R_auto_div) %>% rename(prison_exposure_idw_r_auto_div = idw_r), by = "GEOID20")
```

### IDW within 10 km

The 10 km radius fit best for overdose in the radius search above.

```{r}
#| label: prison-idw-r10
# Adds prison_exposure_idw_r10 (all prisons within 10 km). 
r10 <- n_within(10)
table(r10 > 0)                              # how many PUMAs have any prison within 10 km
# (r10 is the plain count; the same count is in puma_df as num_prisons_within_10km)
puma_df <- puma_df %>% 
  select(-any_of("prison_exposure_idw_r10")) %>%
  left_join(idw_for_R(10) %>% rename(prison_exposure_idw_r10 = idw_r), by = "GEOID20")

cor(puma_df[, c("prison_exposure_idw_r10", "log_pop_density", "pct_pop_rural")], use = "complete.obs")

m_r10   <- feols(as.formula(paste("overdose_rate_puma ~ prison_exposure_idw_r10 +", controls)),
                 data = puma_df, cluster = ~state_fips)
m_cnt10 <- feols(as.formula(paste("overdose_rate_puma ~ num_prisons_within_10km +", controls)),
                 data = puma_df, cluster = ~state_fips)
etable(m13, m_r10, m_cnt10, fitstat = ~ r2 + aic + n)
```

## Rural subset and save

```{r}
#| label: rural-subset
# Rural PUMAs: more than 50% of the population lives in non-metro (RUCA 4-10) tracts.
puma_rural <- puma_df %>% filter(pct_pop_nonmetro > 50)
```

```{r}
#| label: save
# Read these back with GEOID20 and state_fips as text to keep the leading zeros
write_csv(puma_df, "data/final/national_puma_dataset.csv")
write_csv(puma_rural, "data/final/rural_puma_dataset.csv")
```

# Variables {.unnumbered}

| Variable | Meaning | Source |
|----|----|----|
| `GEOID20`, `state_fips` | 7-digit PUMA ID; 2-digit state code | boundary file |
| `STATEFP20`, `PUMACE20`, `NAMELSAD20`, `ALAND20`, `AWATER20`, … | other boundary-file columns (land and water area in m²) | boundary file |
| `total_pop`, `log_pop` | non-institutional population (average over 2020–2024) and its log | IPUMS |
| `pct_nonwhite`, `pct_nonwhite_nh` | \% not White; % not non-Hispanic White | IPUMS |
| `pct_bachelors_plus` | \% of people 25+ with a bachelor's or more | IPUMS |
| `pct_poverty` | \% below the poverty line | IPUMS |
| `pct_unemployed` | \% of the labor force unemployed | IPUMS |
| `medhhinc`, `log_medhhinc` | median household income (2024 \$) and its log | IPUMS |
| `pct_divorced_past_yr` | \% of ever-married people divorced in the past 12 months | IPUMS |
| `pct_divorced_past_yr_atrisk`, `pct_currently_divorced` | alternative divorce measures | IPUMS |
| `n_person_sample`, `n_hh_sample`, `n_divorced_sample` | unweighted sample sizes | IPUMS |
| `overdose_rate_puma` | overdose deaths per 100,000 (2024) | CDC |
| `suicide_rate_puma`, `homicide_rate_puma` | suicide and homicide deaths per 100,000 (2024) | CDC |
| `pct_pop_with_overdose_data`, `n_tracts` | \% of population in tracts with an overdose rate; number of tracts | CDC |
| `pct_pop_metro`, `_micro`, `_small_town`, `_rural`, `pct_pop_nonmetro` | \% of population by RUCA tract type | RUCA |
| `pct_area_nonmetro`, `rural_pop`, `rural_area`, `rural_both` | \% of land area in non-metro tracts; rural flags | RUCA + boundaries |
| `land_area_km2`, `pop_density`, `log_pop_density` | land area; people per km²; log | boundary file + IPUMS |
| `prison_present`, `num_prisons` | any / number of prisons inside the PUMA | prisons |
| `dist_to_nearest_prison_km` | km from the centroid to the nearest prison | prisons |
| `num_prisons_within_5km`, `_10km` | prisons within 5 / 10 km of the centroid | prisons |
| `prison_exposure_idw` | IDW over the 5 nearest prisons | prisons |
| `prison_exposure_idw_auto_od`, `_auto_div` | IDW, K chosen by fit for overdose / divorce | prisons |
| `prison_exposure_idw_r50`, `n_prisons_within_r50` | IDW and count, prisons within 50 km | prisons |
| `prison_exposure_idw_r_auto_od`, `_auto_div` | IDW, radius chosen by fit for overdose / divorce | prisons |
| `prison_exposure_idw_r10` | IDW, prisons within 10 km | prisons |
